sections.title: Policy and access
sections.text:
The big policy in Castelrotto concerns the Seiser Alm, which lies above the village. For summer 2026 the municipality introduced online booking: the municipality announced on 7 May 2026 that all access permits to the Alm except for farm vehicles must be applied for through an online portal, with licence plates checked by camera at five control points [0], and on 19 June 2026 that reservation is required for the car parks P1 Spitzbühl and P2 Compatsch from 29 June 2026, bookable at the earliest six days ahead [3]. The Seiser Alm road is closed to private traffic uphill from 9:00 to 17:00, a valid booking doubles as the access permit, and parking on the Alm is banned from 23:00 to 5:00; the road is open all day when the cable car is closed in the shoulder seasons [4]. Holders of a European Disability Card may drive to Compatsch at any time after registering [7].

The municipality's presentation of 23 April 2026 stated that once both car parks are fully booked no access is possible, and that a barrier at St. Valentin, first considered, was dropped after site visits in Prags [1]. Digital signs in Telfen are planned to show whether P1 and P2 have free spaces, and camera reading is planned at St. Valentin and Compatsch [2]; we found no source confirming that these are running.

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The valley station of the Seiser Alm cable car in Seis has a free open-air car park and two paid garages, Walderer and the new Talstation garage [8], with three public fast EV chargers, one outdoors and one on each garage level; further chargers are listed in Kastelruth, Völs and Tiers [9]. For the Kastelruther Spatzenfest, a very large temporary car park and tent are set up outside the village, free shuttle buses run from three bus stations, and cars are routed around a closed main road [13]. We found no council decision on village parking fees and no new village garage.

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
The Alm car parks are priced to push people onto the cable car: P1 costs 15 euros a car and day and P2 30 euros, the same as the cable car's 30-euro return fare, with day tickets only, payment at booking, no refund and a single entry [5][6]. In the village, the central garage at the bus station is listed at 2.20 euros an hour by day with a daily maximum of 24 euros [10], and the Marinzen lot behind the supermarket at 1.50 euros an hour or a 5-euro day ticket [11]. These come from the tourism association's own, undated listings and name no operator, so treat them as listed offers rather than verified tariffs.

Our data cover two village garages, Centralpark (218 spaces) and the Albin Gross garage (97), from the South Tyrol open-data platform, measured since 27 September 2026. Occupancy averaged about 27% on weekdays and 30% at weekends, weighted by spaces. The Centralpark garage averaged 30% and reached 70%, while the smaller garage averaged 19% and reached full in a single Friday-morning reading. The two cover the village centre, not the Alm car parks, so they say nothing about the booking system. The window is autumn, outside the summer peak.
